Transparent giving for Nigeria

Good evening everyone, my name is Ndujekwu Ugochukwu presenting on behalf of Team Kairos.

Kairos is a transparent crowdfunding platform for people who want to help but need to know what exactly happened to their money. Here, every naira you give can be traced until it reaches the need it was given for.

DELIVERY NOTEIntroduce yourself, then let the promise of traceable giving land.
53 spoken wordsNext: A transfer succeeds. The doubt stays.
02 / 11Ugochukwu

A transfer succeeds. The doubt stays.

Our school fees went up recently and a final year student who couldn't afford it posted an appeal so he wouldn't drop out. People gave. But then more posts appeared and my friends and I started to wonder if they were all real, because the screenshots looked identical and very easy to edit.

Dishonest people have made skepticism the rational response and so potential donors hold back even when the plea is legitimate and real needs go unmet. The missing piece is not compassion. It's a trusted middle layer.

DELIVERY NOTETell the school-fees story in your own voice. Leave a pause before the trusted middle layer.
89 spoken wordsNext: From a published budget to a personal receipt.
03 / 11Ugochukwu

From a published budget to a personal receipt.

Kairos is that trusted middle layer.

First, an AI interviewer helps the organizer explain the need and publish an itemised budget naming the school, hospital or supplier.

Second, the cause is shared as a link, so donors can see the story, budget and payment history. The plan is for a licensed partner to hold donations in escrow and pay only those verified providers, never the organizer's personal account.

Third, every donor gets a receipt showing their own share of each payment.

DELIVERY NOTEThe case, the provider payment, the receipt. Describe licensed custody as the intended live flow.

05 / 11Ugochukwu

Useful to give. Sustainable to run.

Kairos is built to be run, not sold.

We aim to cover running costs through donations and grants from NGOs. Without that support, we'd tentatively take two percent per donation, capped at five thousand naira per cause. Donors see the fee before confirming.

DELIVERY NOTENGO donations and grants are intended support, not secured funding. The upkeep is a tentative fallback; its cap is per cause. The prototype's fee flow does not implement a grant-dependent switch.

Technical approach

The app runs on Next.js and TypeScript. The interview is powered by Claude that helps structure the need and budget for the organiser. We use MongoDB and Cloudinary to store the data.

DELIVERY NOTEBudget: 0:20. Use the supplied wording verbatim.
32 spoken wordsNext: Responsible operation
08 / 11Budget 1:00Ugochukwu

Responsible operation

It is worth reiterating that we store no sensitive data and do not keep any money. When an organiser supplies documents as proof to support their cause the AI model discerns which is safe to display publicly and only does so with their permission.

When a remita reference has expired at payout, we request a replacement and confirm it is the same student, institution and bill, and then proceed to payout.

In the future, we plan to look into more sophisticated ways to reconcile disputes, especially when we move beyond school fees. We aim to make this as automated as possible while remaining accurate.

DELIVERY NOTEBudget: 1:00. Presenter-supplied operating-model wording. Current uploads are stored and published attachments are public. Automated publication review and expired-reference recovery remain planned.

We start with school fees because they're easy to verify in Nigeria. We have spoken with our department bodies that help raise funds for students and have got very a positive response

Then we plan to move to hospitals and other service providers.

10 / 11Ugochukwu

Give with proof, not faith

In short, Kairos turns charitable giving from an act of blind trust into one of complete transparency. We don't claim fraud is impossible. We're building Kairos to make it visible, traceable, capped and unprofitable.

18 of 18 questions
What does Kairos do?Rehearse first001 · The giving flow

It connects a published need and budget to provider payments and each donor's share. The prototype implements the accounting and updates; live custody and settlement still require integration.

What stops the organizer withdrawing donations?Rehearse first002 · The giving flow

The prototype has no personal cash-withdrawal path and checks payment permissions, balance and budget. Live operation needs a licensed custody/payment arrangement that enforces the same restrictions.

Does the receipt independently prove the school received money?Rehearse first003 · The giving flow

The current receipt records a simulated application payout. A live settled receipt must be tied to confirmed provider settlement; a locally generated invoice alone is insufficient.

Can someone give without an account?004 · The giving flow

Yes. Guest gifts are anonymous and appear in the public cause records. Signed-in donors can receive personal in-app updates; email is optional.

What if a Remita reference expires?Rehearse first005 · Review and privacy

The agreed proposed flow pauses payout, asks the organizer through the AI for a replacement, verifies the same student, institution and bill, then continues. This is not yet implemented.

When does a human step in?Rehearse first006 · Review and privacy

The proposed workflow escalates a mismatch or an unresolved check. The reviewer checks evidence, records the decision and permits an appropriate next step. A dedicated reviewer workflow is not built.

Does AI authenticate documents or identify fraud?Rehearse first007 · Review and privacy

It helps structure the need and can discuss consistency. Uploads are accepted supporting material. Independent document authentication, image-reuse checks and live registry checks are not operational.

Who can view supporting files today?Rehearse first008 · Review and privacy

Unpublished files are owner-only. Files attached to published causes are publicly viewable through the app. Sensitive evidence needs a separate access/redaction design before live use.

Do you store a donor's or organizer's NIN?009 · Review and privacy

The current identity endpoint stores the simulated verification result and method, not the NIN number. This does not establish that live identity verification or a complete launch privacy program is in place.

How does the fee cap work?Rehearse first010 · Fees and records

The current rule takes 2% of each gross gift until total upkeep reaches ₦5,000 for that cause. It is a per-cause cap. The charge and net cause credit are shown before confirmation.

How are donor shares calculated?Rehearse first011 · Fees and records

The allocation uses the donor's net contribution after upkeep. In the full school-fee example, Abigail's ₦155,000 gross payment credits ₦153,000 and that net amount is attributed to the school's recorded payout.

Have you reconciled real bank payments?Rehearse first012 · Fees and records

No. Internal balances and payment allocations run in the prototype. External reconciliation needs unique references and a match to confirmed provider settlement, including pending, failed and duplicate events.

Is NGO funding already secured?013 · Fees and records

No. Donations and NGO grants are the intended primary support, with tentative capped upkeep as a fallback. The prototype currently applies its upkeep rule; no grant-triggered switch or proven unit economics is claimed.

Are refunds implemented?014 · Fees and records

A complete production refund and dispute process is still to be designed and integrated. The prototype does not prove that operation.

What user research supports this presentation?Rehearse first015 · Evidence and launch

The school-fee experience and a conversation with the past president of Ugochukwu’s department support the problem statement. He helps raise fees and reported that existing trust does not always make the details easy to verify. This is qualitative problem feedback, not a completed product test or a live pilot. No donor or institution usability findings have been supplied.

What would the first pilot measure?016 · Evidence and launch

Start with school-fee bills settled, donor understanding of receipts, unresolved payment issues and repeat giving. These are proposed measures, not completed pilot results.

What remains before live donations?Rehearse first017 · Evidence and launch

Licensed custody and live payments, independent verification, appropriate private-evidence controls, external reconciliation and an exception/refund process. No signed custody partnership is claimed.

How long is this pitch allowed to be?018 · Evidence and launch

The organizer’s format is one minute for team introduction, seven minutes for presentation and demo, five minutes for questions and two for scoring/transition. This expanded draft deliberately has no delivery schedule yet. Timing will be decided after the content is edited.

Keep these distinctions clear

  • Working: prototype accounting, budget checks, attribution, notifications and public history.
  • Simulated: bank transfer, Remita settlement and NIN lookup.
  • Unbuilt: live CAC and account-name checks, general upload verification and the complete production operating flow.
  • Not signed: licensed custody and payments partnership.
  • User evidence: The presenter reports a positive response from departmental bodies that raise student fees. This is qualitative feedback, not a completed live-money pilot.
